extracted.intended_audience: research evaluators, funders, university administrators, and policymakers designing grant- and research-assessment rubrics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating responsible, metric-informed grant evaluation rubrics that align with institutional missions and avoid the misuse of bibliometric indicators. Emphasizes transparency, field-normalization, qualitative judgment, and periodic review to prevent gaming and perverse incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative evaluation should support qualitative, expert assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers inform but do not replace expert judgment; reviewers should retain authority over final assessment; metrics are inputs to deliberation, not substitutes for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metrics to inform expert panels rather than to deterministically rank or decide. Ensure reviewers understand metric limitations and can override or contextualize metric signals using qualitative evidence (e.g., letters, full portfolio).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure performance against the research missions of the unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Goals should be defined first, metrics chosen to track them; different missions (basic research, applied research, training) require different metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the institution/funder's mission before selecting indicators. Avoid one-size-fits-all metrics; choose indicators that map to stated objectives (e.g., societal impact measures for applied missions, training indicators for educational missions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect excellence in locally relevant research
rubrics_metrics.description: Some excellent research targets local/regional needs; global metrics (international citations) penalize this work; a defensible rubric must accommodate locally important research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design rubrics to recognize local/regional relevance (policy briefs, local-language outputs, regional journals, community engagement) and avoid penalizing work that is important outside global citation streams. Include qualitative evidence of local impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep data collection and analytical processes open, transparent, and simple
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should be able to verify the data; methods should be replicable; black-box assessment is not legitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish data sources, extraction methods, normalization procedures, and any code used. Prefer simple, reproducible indicators over opaque proprietary algorithms. Document assumptions and limitations clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow those evaluated to verify data and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers can access their own metrics; errors can be identified and corrected; evaluation is auditable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide applicants access to the raw data and calculated indicators used in their assessment, a process for correction of errors, and an audit trail of metric calculations and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for variation by field in publication and citation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation rates vary 10x across fields; author count conventions differ; cross-field comparison must use field-normalized metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use field-normalized indicators or discipline-specific benchmarks when comparing researchers across fields. Adjust for authorship conventions (e.g., large collaborations) and typical publication/citation cadence of each discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base assessment of individual researchers on qualitative judgement of their portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't rank individuals by single metrics; use holistic judgment of body of work; weight context (career stage, field, role) appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate full portfolios (publications, grants, supervision, outreach, datasets, software) with narrative context. Consider career breaks, role differences (team leaders vs. collaborators), and stage-appropriate expectations rather than applying raw metric thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misplaced concreteness and false precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics suggest precision they don't have; small numerical differences are not meaningful; 'Top decile' classifications can be misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fine-grained cutoffs based on small metric differences. Present metric ranges or bands and use qualitative confirmation for distinctions. Beware presenting metrics with spurious decimal precision or implying exact rank-order validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the systemic effects of assessment and indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Goodhart's Law applies: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure; researchers will optimize for whatever is measured; assessment criteria shape research itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate behavioral responses to indicators (salami-slicing, citation gaming, venue-targeting). Prefer diverse indicators and rotate or audit measures to reduce perverse incentives. Monitor for emergent gaming strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize indicators regularly and update them
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics that worked in 1990 may not work in 2025; periodically audit whether indicators still measure what they're supposed to; be willing to abandon indicators that have been gamed or have lost validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute scheduled reviews of chosen indicators, validate predictive relevance against desired outcomes, retire or revise metrics that no longer perform, and document changes and rationale publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use metrics as input to expert judgment, not as decision rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics should inform but not determine funding decisions; they should not be used as rigid decision rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design workflows where panels see metric summaries alongside qualitative materials, and require panel narrative justification for decisions, especially when metrics and qualitative evidence conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor criteria to the funding mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant criteria should be aligned to the funder's mission (e.g., basic vs applied; early-career vs established).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify mission-relevant evaluation dimensions (e.g., translational impact for applied grants, training outputs for capacity-building grants) and select indicators and weighting consistent with those priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use field-normalized metrics when comparing across disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: When cross-discipline comparisons are required, use metrics normalized to field publication and citation norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement normalization methods (e.g., percentile ranks, field-specific benchmarks) and avoid raw citation counts as cross-field comparators. Document normalization choices and their limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be auditable and transparent — applicants can see what's being scored
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubrics must be transparent so applicants can verify scoring and understand decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish rubric criteria, indicator definitions, and applicant-specific metric calculations; provide appeals or correction procedures and maintain an auditable record of scoring and panel rationales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid implying precision that doesn't exist (do not over-quantify)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not present metrics as more precise or definitive than they are; avoid spurious exactness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer coarse-grained categories or confidence intervals over exact ranks; explicitly state measurement error and uncertainty; avoid language that suggests metric determinism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate gaming — design criteria robust to optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Design rubrics that are resistant to manipulation and do not create perverse incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine multiple indicators, include qualitative checks, monitor for gaming behaviors, and adjust incentives. Avoid single-number targets that invite optimization at the expense of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodically audit the rubric — does it still predict desired outcomes?
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly evaluate whether the rubric and indicators predict the outcomes the funder values and adjust accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set review cycles, collect validation data (e.g., downstream impact, portfolio success), revise criteria based on evidence, and communicate changes to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using Journal Impact Factor (JIF) as a proxy for individual quality (DORA complement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use journal-level metrics such as JIF to assess individual researchers or individual articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the article/content itself and use article-level or other appropriate indicators; explicitly prohibit use of JIF in applicant evaluation language to align with DORA principles.
